page.title: Choosing a Virtual Summit Platform
page.description: A practical guide to deciding audience outcome, ownership, participation features, cost models and timelines for a virtual summit platform.
page.h1: What should you decide first about a virtual summit platform?
page.definition: A virtual summit platform is software that hosts multi‑session online events with live streaming, registration, networking and analytics, letting organizers deliver content to remote audiences at scale. It also integrates with marketing automation, provides moderated Q&A, and supports hybrid extensions for on‑site components.
page.quick_answer: Pick the audience outcome and format first, then assign a single owner for the run of show before evaluating platform features.

sections.h2: What audience outcome and format should drive the platform choice?

blocks.p: The desired outcome — lead generation, community building, or product education — and the session format — keynote, breakout, workshop — dictate which platform capabilities you need. Start by writing a one‑sentence goal and listing every session type you plan to run.

ul: Map session types to required features (live polls, breakout rooms, networking lounges)
Confirm attendee capacity and geographic distribution
Check integration needs with CRM and marketing automation

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and production?

blocks.p: A single person must own the run of show, rehearse speakers and keep a backup stream ready, because the platform is not the production. Document the owner and the deliverables they are responsible for.

ul: Branded slide template and lower thirds designer

blocks.p: Live polls, moderated Q&A, chat reactions, and virtual networking lounges are the measurable signals that attendees are active. Choose a platform that surfaces these metrics in real time and exports them for post‑event reporting.

sections.h2: How do cost models compare across platform tiers?

blocks.p: Three cost models dominate: per‑host licences sized by attendee capacity, self‑serve monthly plans, and annual contracts quoted by sales. Match the model to your budgeting cycle and the number of events you run each year.

sections.h2: What timeline and staffing are realistic for a summit?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out, lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final, and staff a show caller, speaker manager, moderator and platform operator. Build the schedule backward from the live date.

ul: Six to eight weeks: platform selection, venue AV lock, registration setup
Four to six weeks: speaker briefs, rehearsal schedule, run of show draft
Two to five days before: full rehearsal on real platform
Within twenty four to forty eight hours: replay delivery

faq.q: How early should I book the platform for a virtual summit?
faq.a: Reserve the platform at least six weeks before the event date; this gives time for speaker rehearsals, registration integration, and a full technical run‑through on the actual system. Early booking also secures preferred capacity tiers and avoids last‑minute price surges.

faq.q: What is the difference between a platform licence and a production crew?
faq.a: A platform licence provides the streaming software, registration pages and analytics; a production crew supplies the run of show, camera operators, live director, backup encoder and post‑event editing, which the software alone cannot deliver. Both purchases are required for a polished summit experience.

faq.q: Which participation metrics should I report to stakeholders?
faq.a: Report live poll response rate, Q&A question volume, chat reaction count, networking match connections, and post‑session survey completion; together they show attention depth and conversion potential. Tie each metric to the original summit goal such as lead capture or community growth.

faq.q: Can I run a summit on a platform I already use for webinars?
faq.a: Yes, many teams produce summits on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, the enterprise suite or StreamYard because the familiar interface reduces speaker training time and leverages existing licences. Confirm that the plan supports breakout rooms, networking lounges and the attendee capacity you need.
